notes: Read both tax-policy units, full fiscal context, all twelve candidates and the review. Restored the stated growth purpose to the reported Obama-Democratic tax cuts; retained American-family scope for the no-tax-increase pledge; kept the wealthiest-taxpayer request as President Obama's reported action; resolved the spending cuts and investments; identified the U.S. tax code; and kept loophole closure and reduced offshoring incentives within corporate-tax reform.

claims.claim_text: To spur economic growth, President Obama and the Democratic Party cut taxes for every working family, providing the typical family $3,600 over his first term.
Commitment not to raise taxes on the 98 percent of American families earning less than $250,000 annually.
To reduce the deficit while maintaining needed education, research, infrastructure and clean-energy investments, President Obama asked the wealthiest taxpayers to pay their fair share.
Unneeded federal spending should be cut to make room for investments needed to grow the U.S. economy.
Commitment to make the U.S. tax code fairer and simpler.
Commitment to make the U.S. tax code satisfy the Buffett Rule so no millionaire pays a smaller income share in taxes than middle-class families.
Commitment to reform the corporate tax code by closing loopholes and reducing incentives for corporations to move jobs overseas.
